doc.title: Dave Bailey and John McNeil Interview, 1959-10-25

title: Teaching himself drums on tubs and pans
summary: No teacher: he learned on tubs and boxes, nearly lost his delivery job, and his brother bought a pawn-shop drum set.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Getting my first drums, with or without lessons

blocks.x: Well now, when you were getting started, did you just pick up drums by yourself at first, or did you have a teacher?
No teacher. Just pick it up.
That's at first. Now, about how old were you when you started on drums?
I didn't know. I didn't know then.
Well, were you wearing long pants when you started? Oh no, I was a kid in short pants.
I started out a little bit of something. I started out when I just come up.
About three feet high, so, huh? Something like that.

I learned on tubs, tin pans, and boxes. Oh yeah, I see. Many people would throw the water at night. I'd be on people's step at 12 o'clock at night with some clean sticks. I was working at Old Magazine Market, trying to have the Old Magazine Market. I liked to have lost my job. I was delivering meat.

I got up to fill up in the non-station. He was having to stick in between the collar leg, you know, hold it laid open. They'd pine that these down. I seen a troubled trash. I ended up in the trash in the street. After I lived up with me, he got there and the girl and I was in the truck. I had to run in. And I got back, he says, I bet you've been playing drums. I said, Dave, if I didn't like you, he was a good boy, I'd fire. I said, I'll let this fly. I was about an hour or something back, he's going back.
I kept on trying to learn.

So my brother said, well I'm going to buy a little cheap drum. Cheap set. Went down to the pawn shop and got me a little old cheap snap drum. I got a little old bass drum. I made up a little band and I went on to the store and everything.
